stimuli.text: Initial-rate data for A + B → products:
A student heats 7 g of $$\ce{CaCO3(s)}$$, which decomposes completely: $$\ce{CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g)}$$. The $$\ce{CO2}$$ is collected at 305 K and 0.95 atm.
The decomposition of compound X was monitored at constant temperature.
A student titrates 34.0 mL of 0.13 M weak monoprotic acid HA (Ka = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}) with 0.11 M NaOH.

The photoelectron spectra of C (Z = 6) and N (Z = 7) are compared.

options.text: Ions are fixed in the solid but mobile in the liquid

options.why: Correct. It is most attracted to the nonpolar mobile phase.
Polar components stay with the polar paper.

options.text: A larger fraction of collisions have energy at or above the activation energy

options.why: Correct. E = hc/λ, with λ in meters.

options.text: It is always omitted as a spectator

options.why: Correct. It is a weak acid and mostly un-ionized.

questions.explanation: It is a weak acid and mostly un-ionized.

options.why: With L and atm, use R = 0.08206.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3}$$, $$\ce{H2}$$ is consumed at 0.9 M/s. At what rate does $$\ce{NH3}$$ form?

options.why: Correct. Multiply by the coefficient ratio 2/3.
Divide by the reactant's coefficient too.

questions.stem: 104 g of water at 72 °C is mixed with 95 g of water at 10 °C in an insulated container. What is the final temperature?

options.why: Pair each mass with its own temperature.
Correct. Heat lost = heat gained; for water alone, a mass-weighted average.

questions.stem: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?

options.text: It provides a pathway with a lower activation energy
options.why: Correct. The reaction goes by a different mechanism.

questions.explanation: The reaction goes by a different mechanism.

questions.stem: Which substance has the highest boiling point?

options.why: Correct. Water forms extensive hydrogen bonds.

questions.stem: On a reaction energy profile, the reactants are at 114 kJ/mol, the transition state at 230 kJ/mol and the products at 141 kJ/mol. What is the activation energy of the reverse reaction?

options.why: Measure from the correct starting point.
Correct. Reverse Ea = transition state − products.

questions.explanation: Forward Ea = 116, ΔH = 27, reverse Ea = 89 kJ/mol.

questions.stem: A 37.9 mL sample of $$\ce{H2SO4}$$ is titrated to the equivalence point with 22 mL of 0.209 M NaOH. What is the concentration of the acid?

options.why: Correct. Each H₂SO₄ reacts with two OH⁻, so divide the moles of NaOH by 2.

questions.stem: What is the mass percent of Fe in $$\ce{Fe2O3}$$?

options.why: Use masses, not numbers of atoms.
There are 2 atoms of Fe in the formula.
That is the percent of the other elements.

questions.stem: Which compound has the greater lattice energy, $$\ce{LiF}$$ or $$\ce{BaO}$$?

options.text: $$\ce{LiF}$$, because it has more atoms per formula unit
options.why: Number of atoms does not determine lattice energy.

options.text: $$\ce{LiF}$$, because its ions have larger charges
They are equal because both are ionic
$$\ce{BaO}$$, because its ions have larger charges
options.why: Correct. By Coulomb's law, attraction increases with the product of the ion charges.

questions.explanation: BaO has ion charges 2 and 2; LiF has 1 and 1.

questions.stem: A mass spectrum of a sample of chlorine shows two peaks: mass 35 with relative abundance 38% and mass 37 with 62%. What is the average atomic mass of the sample?

options.why: The isotopes are not equally abundant.
Correct. Weight each isotope mass by its fractional abundance.
Pair each mass with its own abundance.

questions.stem: A 14.1 mL sample of $$\ce{H2SO4}$$ is titrated to the equivalence point with 11.7 mL of 0.125 M NaOH. What is the concentration of the acid?

options.why: Correct. Each H₂SO₄ reacts with two OH⁻, so divide the moles of NaOH by 2.

questions.stem: Two buffers have the same pH, but buffer X has ten times the concentration of each component. Which is true?

options.text: Buffer X cannot resist pH changes
Buffer X has a greater buffer capacity
options.why: Correct. More acid and base are available to react.

options.text: Buffer X has a lower pH
options.why: The ratio, and pH, are the same.

questions.explanation: More acid and base are available to react.

questions.stem: A solution has an absorbance of 1.05 in a 2 cm cuvette. The molar absorptivity is 586 M⁻¹cm⁻¹. What is the concentration?
Samples of $$\ce{O2}$$, $$\ce{He}$$, $$\ce{N2}$$, $$\ce{Cl2}$$ are all at the same temperature. Which has the highest average molecular speed?

options.why: N2 has a larger molar mass (28 g/mol).
O2 has a larger molar mass (32 g/mol).
Cl2 has a larger molar mass (70.9 g/mol).
Correct. At the same temperature, average kinetic energy is equal, so the lightest gas moves fastest.

questions.explanation: Molar masses: O2 32, He 4, N2 28, Cl2 70.9.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{A(g) + B(g) <=> 2C(g)}$$, K = 1.9. A mixture has [A] = 0.4 M, [B] = 0.4 M and [C] = 0.3 M. In which direction will the reaction proceed?

options.text: It proceeds in reverse, toward reactants, because Q = 0.562
options.why: If Q is less than K, the reaction proceeds forward.

options.text: It proceeds forward, toward products, because Q = 0.562
options.why: Correct. Q = [C]²/([A][B]) = 0.562, which is less than K.

options.text: It proceeds forward, toward products, because Q = 1.87
It is at equilibrium, because Q = K

options.text: Reactant and product concentrations are equal

questions.stem: How many valence electrons are shown in the Lewis structure of $$\ce{O3}$$?

options.why: Correct. Sum the valence electrons of all atoms, then add one per negative charge (subtract one per positive charge).

questions.stem: What is the energy of a photon with a wavelength of 405 nm?

options.why: Correct. E = hc/λ, with λ in meters.

questions.stem: A gas mixture contains 0.2 mol N₂, 0.6 mol O₂ and 0.3 mol Ar at a total pressure of 3.5 atm. What is the partial pressure of N₂?

options.why: Use the mole fraction, not moles.
The gases are not present in equal amounts.

questions.stem: A reaction has K = 28. What is K for the reaction reversed and multiplied by 2?

options.why: Correct. Reverse → 1/K; multiply by n → Kⁿ.
K is raised to a power, not multiplied.
Multiplying by n raises K to the nth power.

Make the oxidation numbers add up to the overall charge.

Make the oxidation numbers add up to the overall charge.

questions.stem: A weak acid HA has pKa = 3.7. In a solution at pH 0.9, which statement is correct?

options.why: Correct. Below the pKa, the protonated form dominates.

questions.stem: Samples of $$\ce{O2}$$, $$\ce{H2}$$, $$\ce{Ar}$$, $$\ce{He}$$ are all at the same temperature. Which has the highest average molecular speed?

options.why: He has a larger molar mass (4 g/mol).
Ar has a larger molar mass (40 g/mol).

Correct. At the same temperature, average kinetic energy is equal, so the lightest gas moves fastest.

options.why: Bonds formed release energy: subtract them.
Multiply each bond energy by the number of bonds.
Broken minus formed, not formed minus broken.

options.why: Correct. Doubling [A] multiplies the rate by 1; doubling [B] multiplies it by 1.
Recheck how the rate changes when [A] doubles.
Orders are found from the data, not from coefficients.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O}$$, 8 g of $$\ce{H2}$$ reacts with 77 g of $$\ce{O2}$$. What mass of $$\ce{H2O}$$ can form?

options.why: Apply the mole ratio from the equation.
Not all of both reactants reacts.
Correct. H2 is the limiting reactant.
Use the limiting reactant, which gives less product.

questions.stem: When does a battery's cell potential reach zero?

options.text: When the reaction reaches equilibrium (Q = K)
options.why: Correct. No net driving force remains.

questions.stem: 29 mL of 0.16 M weak acid HA is titrated with 0.24 M NaOH. What volume of NaOH reaches the equivalence point?

options.why: Correct. Moles of base = moles of acid.

questions.stem: For the galvanic cell made from these half-cells, what is ΔG°? (F = 96,485 C/mol)

options.why: Correct. ΔG° = −nFE° with n = 2 electrons transferred and E° = 0.46 V.
ΔG° is negative for a positive E°.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{H2(g) + I2(g) <=> 2HI(g)}$$, initial [H₂] = 1.8 M and [I₂] = 1 M, with no HI. At equilibrium, [HI] = 1.58 M. What is K?
A photoelectron spectrum shows 4 peaks. From highest to lowest binding energy, their relative heights are 2 : 2 : 6 : 1. Which element is it?

options.why: Correct. The peaks correspond to $$1s^{2}\,2s^{2}\,2p^{6}\,3s^{1}$$, which has 11 electrons.

questions.stem: When a reaction involving 0.053 mol of limiting reactant occurs in 55 g of solution (c = 4.18 J/(g·°C)), the temperature rises by 3.1 °C. What is ΔH for the reaction?

options.why: A temperature rise means the reaction is exothermic (negative ΔH).
Divide by the moles of reactant.
Correct. q(solution) = mcΔT = 713 J; q(reaction) = −q(solution); divide by moles.

questions.stem: What is the pH of a 0.1 M solution of hydrofluoric acid (Ka = 6.8 \times 10^{-4})?

options.why: Correct. Solve Ka = x²/(C − x) for x = [H₃O⁺].
A weak acid does not ionize completely.

questions.stem: At 298 K, ΔG° for a reaction is 13 kJ/mol. What is K?

options.why: Correct. K = e^(−ΔG°/RT), with ΔG° in J/mol and R = 8.314.

questions.explanation: ln K = -5.25; K = 5.26 \times 10^{-3}. Positive ΔG°: K less than 1.

questions.stem: The first four ionization energies of an element are 493, 2958, 4230, 7022 kJ/mol. In which group of the periodic table is the element most likely found?

options.why: Correct. The large jump comes after removing 1 electron, so it has 1 valence electron.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.

questions.explanation: The big jump marks the start of removing core electrons.

questions.stem: Reaction 1 has ΔH₁ = -318 kJ and reaction 2 has ΔH₂ = 5 kJ. A target reaction is obtained by doubling reaction 1 and reversing reaction 2. What is ΔH for the target reaction?

options.why: Correct. Reverse → change sign; multiply → multiply ΔH; then add.
Enthalpies add; they do not multiply.
Reversing changes the sign of ΔH₂.

questions.stem: What is the pH of a 0.5 M solution of hydrofluoric acid (Ka = 6.8 \times 10^{-4})?

options.why: Correct. Solve Ka = x²/(C − x) for x = [H₃O⁺].
A weak acid does not ionize completely.

questions.stem: Calculate ΔH° for $$\ce{2C2H6 + 7O2 -> 4CO2 + 6H2O(g)}$$. (ΔH°f of O₂ is 0.)

options.why: Multiply each ΔH°f by its coefficient.
Correct. Σ n ΔH°f(products) − Σ n ΔH°f(reactants).

options.why: Correct. Set ΔG = 0: T = ΔH/ΔS (with ΔH in J).
Convert ΔH to J (or ΔS to kJ).

parts.prompt: Calculate the number of moles of CO₂ produced.

parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of CO₂ expected.

rubric.example: Incomplete decomposition (not heated long enough) or gas leaking from the apparatus.

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a complete Lewis diagram for CO₂, and identify its molecular geometry and the hybridization of carbon.

rubric.example: O=C=O with two lone pairs on each O (16 valence electrons).

parts.prompt: Explain why CO₂ is nonpolar even though C=O bonds are polar.

rubric.criterion: Linear symmetry makes the bond dipoles cancel.

parts.prompt: CaO is an ionic solid. Explain, using Coulomb's law, why CaO has a higher melting point than KCl.

rubric.criterion: Larger ion charges in CaO (2+/2−) than in KCl (1+/1−).
Greater electrostatic attraction (and smaller ions) means more energy is needed to separate the ions.

parts.prompt: Calculate the average rate of disappearance of X between 0 and 20 s.

rubric.example: Equal time intervals give equal changes in ln[X].

parts.prompt: Write the rate law and determine the rate constant, with units.
Calculate the half-life of the reaction (for the initial concentration).
A proposed mechanism has a slow first step: X → Y + Z. Is the mechanism consistent with the rate law? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Yes; the slow step's elementary rate law matches the observed rate law.

parts.prompt: A catalyst is added. Explain its effect on the rate and on the rate constant, using activation energy.

rubric.example: The catalyst provides a new pathway.

rubric.criterion: Lower activation energy means a larger fraction of collisions are successful.

rubric.criterion: Indicator whose pKa is closest to the equivalence pH.

parts.prompt: Explain why the solution at the half-equivalence point resists pH change when a small amount of HCl is added.

rubric.criterion: A⁻ reacts with added H⁺ to form HA (buffer).
rubric.example: A⁻ + H₃O⁺ → HA + H₂O, so the ratio [A⁻]/[HA] changes only slightly.

parts.prompt: Is the dissolution endothermic or exothermic? Justify.

rubric.example: Exothermic: the solution warmed, so energy was released.

parts.prompt: Calculate the heat absorbed or released by the solution.
Calculate ΔH of dissolution in kJ/mol.
If some heat escaped to the surroundings, would the magnitude of the calculated ΔH be too large or too small? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Too small, because the measured temperature change is smaller than the true change.

parts.prompt: Write the balanced net ionic equation for the cell reaction.
Calculate E°cell.
Calculate ΔG° for the cell reaction.
The concentration of Ni²⁺ is increased to 2.0 M. Predict the effect on the cell potential and justify.

rubric.criterion: E decreases because Q increases (a product's concentration rises).
rubric.example: Q greater than 1 → E less than E°.

questions.title: Solubility of a slightly soluble salt

parts.prompt: Write the Ksp expression.
Calculate the molar solubility in pure water.
Calculate the molar solubility in a solution containing 0.1 M OH⁻ (from a soluble salt).
Explain how lowering the pH affects the solubility.

rubric.criterion: Correct reasoning about whether the anion is basic.
rubric.example: Solubility increases: H⁺ reacts with OH⁻ (a base), shifting the equilibrium toward dissolving.

parts.prompt: Write the electron configuration of N.
Explain why the 1s peak of N has a higher binding energy than the 1s peak of C.

rubric.criterion: N has more protons, so 1s electrons are attracted more strongly (Coulomb's law).

parts.prompt: Describe one difference in the number or relative height of peaks between the two spectra.

rubric.criterion: A valid difference based on configurations.
rubric.example: N has one more electron, so its outermost peak is taller or an extra peak appears.

parts.prompt: Which element has the larger atomic radius? Justify using Coulomb's law.

rubric.criterion: C: fewer protons with similar shielding, so valence electrons are held less tightly.
rubric.example: Same period; effective nuclear charge increases across.
